records.name: Czechia
records.summary_text:
Czechia is broadly workable with an improving trajectory and a major welcoming tourist hub (Prague), offset by unprepared detention systems and elevated baseline social hostility. If detained, the system is unprepared: a documented case shows police mishandling the extradition-detention of an HIV-positive trans foreigner; safeguards ordered at the highest court level exist, but practice is inconsistent.

About half of LGBTIQ people report being targeted by insults, assault or threats over five years, and a far-right party uses "deviant" rhetoric; Prague and larger cities are welcoming,

records.name: Slovenia
records.summary_text:
Slovenia is among Central and Eastern Europe's most progressive destinations for trans visitors, with a cleaner documented profile than its neighbours. Legal gender recognition is depathologised (no surgery or psychiatric-diagnosis requirement), and a 2022 reform abolished local jurisdiction in the gender-change procedure — reducing involuntary outing through local bureaucracy. Comprehensive anti-discrimination law covers gender identity, same-sex marriage is legal (2022, via the Constitutional Court), and no far-right party is in government.

No severe traveler-axis incidents surfaced
